notes.meaning: Humanity began to multiply quickly across the face of the earth, and many daughters were born into these families. While growth in population was part of God's original blessing, sinful human nature turned this blessing into an occasion for greater rebellion. As the number of people grew, their separation from God grew along with it.

differ.view: Some hold that the sons of God were fallen angels who took human bodies and married human women to corrupt the human race.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic commentators reject the Sethite view because daughters of men naturally means humanity in general, and note that these unions occurred both before and after the flood.

notes.meaning: Men called the 'sons of God'—traditionally understood as the godly family line of Seth—chose wives from ungodly families based only on outward physical beauty. They followed their own desires rather than seeking God's will for marriage. These mixed marriages caused true religion to fade and led to widespread moral decay.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe the 'sons of God' were fallen angels who took on physical human forms and married human women.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: A Catholic perspective rejects the view that these were marriages between Seth's and Cain's lines, noting that the text refers to humanity in general and that these unions occurred both before and after the flood.

notes.meaning: The Lord announced that His Holy Spirit would not plead with and restrain rebellious humanity forever. Since people are mortal and bent on earthly desires, God set a limit on His patience. He granted humanity a 120-year period of grace to repent before the coming judgment.

differ.view: Some evangelicals understand the 120 years as a newly reduced limit on the normal human lifespan rather than a countdown to the flood.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars translate the verb as 'abide' rather than 'strive,' arguing that God was declaring His breath of life would no longer remain in humans past an age of 120 years.

notes.meaning: Powerful, violent men known as the Nephilim lived on the earth during this era, using their strength to terrorize and dominate others. The children born from these ungodly unions became famous heroes and warriors of old. Their lasting fame came from lawless power and oppression rather than goodness before God.

differ.view: Some evangelicals teach that the Nephilim were the literal, unnatural offspring produced when fallen angels mated with human women.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: A popular modern theory claims the Nephilim were alien visitors or mythic monsters, though conservative Bible teachers point out they were actual human warriors of great size and violent power.

notes.meaning: God saw how widespread human wickedness had become across the world. Sin was not just an outward act, but had thoroughly infected the human heart, which is the center of a person's thoughts and motives. Every desire and plan of mankind was completely and constantly bent on evil.

The Lord felt deep sorrow in His heart over the terrible wickedness of humanity. This does not mean God makes mistakes or changes His mind like a human does. Instead, it describes God's holy pain and righteous grief when His good creation abandons Him for sin.

The Lord announced that He would completely wipe out mankind, along with land animals, crawling creatures, and birds. Because humanity was given authority over creation, the animal kingdom shared in the earthly ruin caused by human sin. God's holiness demanded a complete wiping away of this corrupt world.

Amidst a world headed for destruction, Noah found favor and mercy in the sight of the Lord. God looked upon Noah with kindness when the rest of humanity was entirely corrupt. This marked a ray of divine hope that a faithful remnant would be preserved.

differ.view: Reformed Christians emphasize that Noah found favor solely through God's free election and unmerited grace, which then produced godliness in him, rather than because of any personal human merit.
Methodists teach that Noah obtained favor because he responded to God through repentance and active faith, receiving the inner witness of being made righteous.

notes.meaning: Noah was an upright man who lived with moral integrity among the corrupt people of his generation. Calling him blameless does not mean he was entirely sinless, but that he was sincere and devoted in doing God's will. Like Enoch before him, Noah walked in close daily fellowship with God.

differ.view: Some hold that blameless in his generations means Noah's physical bloodline remained pure from demonic intermarriage.

notes.meaning: Noah became the father of three sons named Shem, Ham, and Japheth. These three sons would join Noah in the ark and be preserved through the coming flood. Through them and their wives, God would rebuild the human family in the new world.

Human society had decayed into utter corruption before God's watchful eyes and was filled with lawless violence. People showed complete contempt for God's worship and trampled on each other through murder, robbery, and oppression. Without the fear of God, human life had become cruel and unsafe.

God looked down upon the earth and personally observed its condition, confirming that everyone had turned to evil. Corruption was not limited to a few people, but had spread to the entire human race. People had thoroughly ruined the holy and good way of life God intended for them.

God revealed to Noah that the time had arrived to bring an end to all living creatures because the earth was overflowing with violence. The decision of divine justice was final and could no longer be delayed. God announced that He would destroy both the wicked inhabitants and the earthly realm they had defiled.

God instructed Noah to build a massive vessel out of gopher wood, which was likely durable cypress. He was to construct rooms or cabins inside it and coat the entire vessel inside and out with tar to keep it watertight. This ark was not designed to sail like a ship, but to float safely and preserve life upon the rising waters.

God provided the exact measurements for constructing the ark: three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. Based on standard measurements, this formed a massive rectangular barge roughly 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet tall. Its enormous capacity provided plenty of room for all the inhabitants and their supplies.

Noah was directed to place an opening for light and air around the top of the ark, finishing it about eighteen inches below the roof. He was also to construct a single door in the side and build the interior with lower, middle, and upper decks. These three levels allowed the living creatures and provisions to be organized properly.

The Lord declared that He Himself was bringing a great deluge of waters to cover the earth. Every living creature under the sky that possessed the breath of life would die in this judgment. Outside the safety of the ark, nothing on dry ground would survive the flood.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars propose that the flood was a severe local inundation covering only the ancient Near East rather than the entire globe.

notes.meaning: God promised to establish His covenant, a binding divine agreement, with Noah. Under this promise, Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives were assured safe entry and preservation inside the ark. This covenant gave Noah strong assurance that God would remain faithful to him throughout the coming storm.

Noah was commanded to bring a pair of every kind of animal—one male and one female—into the ark to keep them alive. God chose to protect and preserve His existing animal creation rather than creating new species after the flood. This guaranteed that every animal kind would survive to repopulate the earth.

Pairs of every kind of bird, large land animal, and small crawling creature would come directly to Noah to be saved. Noah did not need to track down and capture all these animals by himself, because God would direct them to the ark. God took care of gathering the creatures so that their kinds would continue.

Noah was instructed to gather and store every sort of food that could be eaten by humans and animals. This large storehouse of supplies would nourish everyone on board throughout their long stay on the water. God commanded ordinary planning and work alongside His miraculous protection.

Noah obeyed God completely, doing everything precisely as the Lord commanded him. Despite the enormous labor, the long years of building, and the likely laughter of his neighbors, Noah persevered in faith. His steady obedience showed that he genuinely trusted God's warnings about things not yet seen.
